Inter-rater agreement report

ElectroClean 1.0.0 · 3 recording(s) · annotators: A01, A02, A03 · label catalogue electroclean-hed-score-artifacts 1.0.0

How to read this report. Agreement is reported along three dimensions: category (do annotators use the same artifact type?), time (do they mark the same parts of the recording?) and channels (do they mark the same channels?). Most EEG is clean, so two annotators agree on most of the recording simply by both leaving it unmarked. Overall proportion agreement is therefore dominated by clean data and is not a useful headline. Read positive agreement (agreement about where artifacts are) together with negative agreement and kappa, the prevalence of each category, and the event-based F1, rather than any single number. Kappa is low when a category is rare even if annotators mostly agree (see the prevalence and bias indices). Units of time are not independent, so no confidence intervals are given for time-resolved statistics.

5. Channel-specific agreement

In time-and-channel mode every channel is analysed separately and the results are pooled (units: channel-seconds or channel-bins). Whole-montage annotations count for every channel of the recording. Event matching additionally requires the events to share channels; the channel Jaccard index of matched events measures how similar the channel selections were.
